keyFindings.description: Security[secret]: the round-2 mask stops at the four address keys; `runtime.kubernetes.plugins.pi_legion`/`pi_envoy` are emitted verbatim on the unauthenticated route while `readPluginSource` (config/kubernetes.go:359-363) admits any http(s) URL with a host and stores `u.String()` with userinfo, query and fragment intact — the one URL-shaped key the loader puts no credential rule on (agent_secrets.url refuses userinfo at kubernetes.go:275; the four address keys refuse a query at config.go:788-793). docs/kubernetes.md:1083-1090 names the http(s) URL as a first-class source (a private or pre-signed tarball), so a basic-auth or pre-signed credential loads and is served to anything that reaches the API port, which under runtime: kubernetes is not loopback. Fix in this PR: either refuse userinfo/query/fragment in readPluginSource as agent_secrets.url does (a contract change: add its census row with the rollout line), or mask the URL form only in kubernetesSettingsOf (endpointOf keeps the path a tarball needs but not a query, so the query must be dropped too; the exact-version and absolute-path forms must pass through unchanged); either way plant a credential-bearing pi_legion URL in settingsFixtureFile and its literal in settingsFixturePlanted so the byte sweep covers the key.

The new doc clause `each address it emits is endpointOf its value` is false: agent_secrets.url (:298) and the plugins pair (:301) never see endpointOf. Comments in this file are the specification the next reader edits against; state the rule (the four address keys ride endpointOf; agent_secrets.url needs none because the loader refuses userinfo on it; the plugins pair's status once the finding above is settled). Ride with the fix.

The cross-language fixture sweep checks state.json for `BEGIN .*PRIVATE KEY` and `postgres://` only and was not extended with the userinfo shape; the Go sweep and Stage 1 cover it, so this is lost redundancy — one `not.toMatch(/:\/\/[^/@\s]+:[^/@\s]+@/)` beside the two lines.

Nothing a reader of the state can reach says the address keys ride with userinfo masked as `xxxxx@`, so an operator seeing `envoy_url: http://xxxxx@…` cannot learn why it differs from the file; one clause in the running-legion bullet (and the version.go 35 entry) closes it.

notProvenRisk: `runtime.kubernetes.plugins.pi_legion`/`pi_envoy` may be an http(s) tarball URL (docs/kubernetes.md:1083-1090); the loader admits userinfo, query and fragment on it (kubernetes.go:359-363) and `settings` emits it verbatim, so a private or pre-signed tarball credential is served on the unauthenticated route (round 2 finding).

The route's reachability beyond Legion's own pods is the deployment's NetworkPolicy, which this repository does not ship; the block describes the deployment's topology (namespace, image digest, scheduling, App ids and installation ids, broker URL and audience) to whatever reaches the API port.
The daemon/image lockstep at contract 35 (a daemon at 35 refuses an image at 34 at its boot gate) was not exercised in either round; the production check is its first run.
